Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. Legal routed us to follow up on two items before we can sign:

1) A firm commitment that Redwood will not use Medisync production data to improve, fine-tune, or otherwise train models (no-training / non-adaptive processing).
2) Operational evidence showing how that commitment is enforced across subprocessors and runtime stacks (attestation, logs, and subprocessor inventory).

We'd like to see:
- Draft DPA redline with explicit "no-training" language (we've included suggested wording in the attached Doc).
- A current subprocessor list with regions and roles.
- A short ops checklist that explains how requests are routed, KV/prefix caching behavior, and where telemetry is stored.

Can you share a redline and the attachments by EOD Tuesday PST? If there's a standard artifact pack you provide for customers (attestation letter, ops checklist, sample logs), that would be perfect.

Best,
Sara

Stephanie / team — drafting note and ops artifacts. High level approach below; I'll attach the checklist and subprocessor CSV in my next send.

Operational commitments we can provide (summary):
- Non-adaptive processing: we will not use Medisync production inputs or outputs to train or update models. Technical enforcement: request headers include tenant id; model training ingest pipelines ignore any data flagged with customer_opt_out metadata.
- KV/prefix caching: KV entries for Medisync tenants are ephemeral and do not feed back into training pipelines; we will document TTLs and eviction policies in the ops checklist.
- Telemetry and logs: request-level telemetry is retained for 30 days for billing and troubleshooting; audit logs for access to production data are retained for 1 year. We can provide an export (redacted) showing the schema and sample rows.
- Subprocessors: current list attached. Any subprocessors outside the US will be flagged in the inventory.

Attachments forthcoming: subprocessors_inventory.csv (export), no-train_ops_checklist.pdf (walkthrough), attestation_letter.pdf (one-page signed).

I'll also propose a small customer-facing paragraph that can be embedded in the DPA: "Redwood will not use Customer production inputs or outputs to improve or train models. Redwood's training pipelines are logically and physically segregated from serving infrastructure; customer data used for billing and debugging is redacted and excluded from training ingestion."

I'll circulate the attachments in an hour.

— David Kim
VP, Platform Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
